title: Dev Flow assurance methodology pool
scope_note: Broad, extensible coverage of established software, systems, UX, operations, and AI-agent implementation methods. It is not a claim to enumerate every method ever published.

global_negative_rules.reason: Low-risk routine work does not justify specialist formal methods without another explicit high-consequence failure signal.
Live or production experiments remain excluded without explicit authority; use the method fallback and report NOT RUN.

selection_contract.rule: Select phase foundations, then matched risk-model methods within depth and context cap. Specialist methods require formal depth and an explicit matching signal. Negative signals suppress selection. Missing prerequisites produce an unresolved method and fallback, never assurance.

methods.name: Repository evidence first
methods.summary: Resolve actual roots, instructions, call paths, contracts, and native controls before choosing a solution.
methods.positive_trigger: Any repository-scoped task.
methods.negative_trigger: Purely conceptual work with no repository claim.
methods.evidence: Exact paths, commands, revisions, and observed behavior.
methods.fallback: Mark unobservable facts unknown and stop affected decisions.
methods.limitations: Static evidence cannot prove device, deployment, or production behavior.

methods.name: Semantic baseline and ambiguity ledger
methods.summary: Persist the current understood meaning, decisions, invariants, and unresolved interpretations before implementation.
methods.positive_trigger: Any persistent behavior change or material ambiguity.
methods.negative_trigger: Read-only fact retrieval with no behavior decision.
methods.evidence: Approved requirement bytes and stable acceptance IDs.
methods.fallback: Use a bounded safe assumption only when reversible and non-material; otherwise ask the owner.
methods.limitations: A digest proves continuity, not requirement correctness.

methods.name: Architecture decision record
methods.summary: Compare credible alternatives and preserve the selected boundary, consequences, and reopening triggers.
methods.positive_trigger: A material type, boundary, state, ownership, compatibility, or resource decision.
methods.negative_trigger: A local implementation detail with an established analogue and no consequential tradeoff.
steps: compare at least two credible options
methods.evidence: Repository anchors and explicit cost/risk comparison.
methods.fallback: Use a reversible spike when decisive evidence is missing.
methods.limitations: A record does not validate the chosen architecture.

methods.name: Coherent vertical slice
methods.summary: Implement the smallest end-to-end behavior slice with its tests, docs, errors, and cleanup together.
methods.positive_trigger: Any persistent implementation.
methods.negative_trigger: A read-only audit or disposable isolated spike.
steps: edit owning path and affected consumers
audit diff and drift before next slice
methods.evidence: Change-set trace and fresh narrow checks.
methods.fallback: Reduce the slice or reopen design when it cannot be verified coherently.
methods.limitations: Small size alone does not make a slice conceptually coherent.

methods.name: Hypothesis-led debugging
methods.summary: Compete evidence-bearing causal hypotheses and intervene on one relevant factor at a time instead of layering speculative repairs.
methods.positive_trigger: A failure, flake, hang, crash, unexplained anomaly, or Agent outcome with several plausible prompt/context/tool/environment/model causes.
methods.negative_trigger: A known deterministic change with no observed defect.
steps: preserve first failure and environment identity
state competing hypotheses across code context tool environment model and infrastructure as applicable
run the cheapest one-factor discriminating intervention
repair only the supported cause and recheck alternatives
methods.evidence: Reproduction and controlled experiments that reject material alternatives.
methods.fallback: After three failed attempts reopen reproduction, model, design, environment, oracle, or authority.
methods.limitations: Correlation, self-explanation, and five-whys narrative are not causal proof; interventions can alter the task.

methods.name: Black-box, white-box, and oracle accounting
methods.summary: Derive observable and structural obligations separately and challenge whether each oracle fails for the target defect.
methods.positive_trigger: Any non-trivial behavior change.
methods.negative_trigger: No behavior claim and no affected executable path, with a concrete reason.
steps: derive white-box cases from changed branches and states
methods.evidence: Executed cells mapped to acceptance and changed structure.
methods.fallback: Keep the evidence gap open; do not call a green but insensitive test sufficient.
methods.limitations: Coverage metrics cannot replace a defect-sensitive oracle.

methods.name: Clean-context blue/red review
methods.summary: Review frozen intent and bytes independently for specification/integration quality and adversarial failure while minimizing shared solution narrative.
methods.positive_trigger: Governed or materially risky change, or explicit independent review.
methods.negative_trigger: Unfrozen work where review findings would immediately become stale.
steps: freeze neutral intent evidence obligations and bytes without implementation advocacy
review requirement integration and maintenance from source evidence
attack failure misuse and rollback hypotheses independently
adjudicate findings and recheck repairs against current bytes
methods.evidence: Finding-specific source and verification evidence plus reviewer/context/model diversity disclosure.
methods.fallback: Root performs the always-on basic challenge and explicitly reports weakened independence.
methods.limitations: Shared specification, model family, context, tools, or prior conclusions create common-mode error even with separate reviewer labels.

methods.name: Acceptance traceability and evidence closure
methods.summary: Close each approved claim with fresh evidence, limitations, and explicit unrun external gates.
methods.positive_trigger: Any completion or acceptance claim.
methods.negative_trigger: Exploratory work that makes no completion claim.
steps: map every acceptance and verification ID
confirm evidence is fresh for final bytes
separate passed failed blocked waived and not run
methods.evidence: Exact commands, environments, artifacts, and limitations.
methods.fallback: Downgrade the claim or leave acceptance blocked.
methods.limitations: Local evidence cannot close an external gate.

methods.name: Operational readiness and rollback contract
methods.summary: Bind target, compatibility, observation, rollback or roll-forward, ownership, and stop conditions before delivery.
methods.positive_trigger: An authorized release, migration, deployment, hotfix, or rollback action.
methods.negative_trigger: Implementation or release planning without delivery authority.
methods.evidence: Executable recovery proof and authorized target.
methods.fallback: Block delivery while preserving implementation readiness.
methods.limitations: A plan does not prove production behavior or authorization.

methods.name: Observability plus USE analysis
methods.summary: Define useful signals and examine utilization, saturation, and errors for each constrained resource.
methods.positive_trigger: A running service or resource/performance claim with observable operations.
methods.negative_trigger: Pure static library behavior with no operational surface.
methods.evidence: Representative telemetry at defined observation points.
methods.fallback: Add bounded instrumentation or keep the operational claim unverified.
methods.limitations: Telemetry reveals symptoms and correlations, not automatically root cause.

methods.name: Stakeholder and outcome mapping
methods.summary: Identify actors, decision owners, affected groups, outcomes, harms, and evidence of success.
methods.positive_trigger: Multiple actors, permissions, conflicting outcomes, or unclear success.
methods.negative_trigger: A bounded technical repair with known actor and observable result.
methods.evidence: Actor-specific acceptance and named owners.
methods.fallback: Record unknown stakeholders as discovery risk.
methods.limitations: A map is a hypothesis until supported by research or domain evidence.

methods.name: User research and prototype testing
methods.summary: Test problem and interaction assumptions with representative users before high-fidelity implementation.
methods.positive_trigger: Material user-facing flow or uncertain user need.
methods.negative_trigger: UI-preserving implementation with established design truth and no new interaction.
methods.evidence: Observed task behavior and decision-linked findings.
methods.fallback: Use heuristic/proxy review and label absence of real-user evidence.
methods.limitations: Small studies find issues but do not statistically prove population outcomes.

methods.name: Journey map and service blueprint
methods.summary: Connect user-visible steps to backstage systems, handoffs, data, failure, and recovery.
methods.positive_trigger: A multi-step or cross-channel journey with handoffs and recovery states.
methods.negative_trigger: A local component with no user journey or service handoff.
methods.evidence: Trace from user outcome to system ownership and acceptance.
methods.fallback: Build a bounded flow/state map from repository evidence.
methods.limitations: Diagrams become stale unless tied to current contracts.

methods.name: Assumption mapping and pre-mortem
methods.summary: Rank uncertain high-impact premises and imagine plausible failure before committing to a design.
methods.positive_trigger: Important decisions depend on unverified premises or large blast radius.
methods.negative_trigger: All consequential premises are already directly evidenced and reversible.
steps: turn top items into evidence tasks
methods.evidence: Each top assumption has owner, test, and invalidation condition.
methods.fallback: Keep the premise explicit and narrow the change.
methods.limitations: Brainstormed risks are not likelihood estimates or proof.

methods.name: Domain storytelling and event storming
methods.summary: Discover domain events, commands, actors, policies, boundaries, and temporal vocabulary collaboratively.
methods.positive_trigger: Complex domain flow, disputed terminology, many actors/events, or cross-boundary state.
methods.negative_trigger: Simple technical transformation with stable domain language.
methods.evidence: Examples trace into requirements and repository contracts.
methods.fallback: Extract events from code/docs and mark domain validation pending.
methods.limitations: Workshop consensus can still encode a wrong domain model.

methods.name: Ubiquitous language and semantic glossary
methods.summary: Bind terms, synonyms, homonyms, units, null/unknown states, and context-specific meanings.
methods.positive_trigger: The same word has multiple meanings or interfaces use inconsistent terms.
methods.negative_trigger: A local change uses established unambiguous vocabulary.
methods.evidence: Terms are used consistently in AC/SC/contracts/tests.
methods.fallback: Keep ambiguous terms qualified by context.
methods.limitations: A glossary does not model identity or lifecycle by itself.

methods.name: Ontology and identity ledger
methods.summary: Define entities, value objects, identifiers, equivalence, lifecycle, aliases, provenance, and cross-boundary identity.
methods.positive_trigger: Multiple identifiers, merges/splits, aliases, tenant boundaries, temporal identity, or migration coexistence.
methods.negative_trigger: Identity is local, immutable, single-source, and unchanged.
steps: map creation merge split delete and alias states
methods.evidence: Examples and invariants distinguish same object from same value.
methods.fallback: Freeze conservative identity assumptions and prohibit lossy merge/migration.
methods.limitations: Ontology models meaning; storage keys alone are not identity proof.

methods.name: Specification by example and example mapping
methods.summary: Use concrete examples, rule/example/question maps, and executable acceptance language to expose semantic gaps.
methods.positive_trigger: Rules have edge cases, exceptions, or competing interpretations.
methods.negative_trigger: A purely structural refactor with proven behavior preservation and no rule change.
methods.evidence: Examples discriminate plausible wrong interpretations.
methods.fallback: Generate repository-derived examples and mark domain confirmation pending.
methods.limitations: Examples do not prove completeness over an unbounded input space.

methods.name: Decision table
methods.summary: Enumerate combinations of conditions, actions, impossible cells, and precedence for rule-dense behavior.
methods.positive_trigger: Multiple boolean/categorical conditions determine behavior.
methods.negative_trigger: A single unconditional rule or continuous numeric relation is better expressed as an invariant/property.
methods.evidence: Every feasible rule maps to an outcome and test.
methods.fallback: Use pairwise combinations if the full table is too large and state omissions.
methods.limitations: Stateful order and temporal progress require a state/temporal model.

methods.name: State transition model
methods.summary: Define states, events, guards, actions, forbidden transitions, terminal states, retries, cancellation, and recovery.
methods.positive_trigger: Behavior depends on lifecycle, event order, retry, cancellation, or recovery.
methods.negative_trigger: Stateless pure transformation with no observable lifecycle.
methods.evidence: Every transition and forbidden edge has an oracle.
methods.fallback: Use a bounded transition table without a modeling tool.
methods.limitations: A state machine alone may not capture concurrency or fairness.

methods.name: Quality attribute scenario
methods.summary: Express stimulus, source, environment, artifact, response, and measurable response for non-functional requirements.
methods.positive_trigger: A performance, reliability, security, modifiability, or compatibility claim affects design.
methods.negative_trigger: No material quality attribute is changed or claimed.
methods.evidence: Representative measurement against a declared threshold.
methods.fallback: Use an observable qualitative boundary and label missing measurement.
methods.limitations: A threshold without representative workload/environment can mislead.

methods.name: Use, misuse, and abuse cases
methods.summary: Model intended goals alongside accidental misuse and intentional abuse at the same boundary.
methods.positive_trigger: Untrusted actors/input, authorization, safety, fraud, or consequential misuse.
methods.negative_trigger: Closed trusted transformation with no meaningful misuse surface.
methods.evidence: Controls and errors are exercised at trust boundaries.
methods.fallback: Record threat-boundary uncertainty and apply conservative validation.
methods.limitations: Scenario enumeration does not prove attack completeness.

methods.name: Invariants and Design by Contract
methods.summary: State preconditions, postconditions, invariants, ownership, and failure semantics at consequential boundaries.
methods.positive_trigger: Correctness depends on stable boundary assumptions or data/state invariants.
methods.negative_trigger: Trivial glue already enforced by language types and unchanged contracts.
methods.evidence: Negative and property tests violate each contract deliberately.
methods.fallback: Document and test the invariant when direct encoding is unavailable.
methods.limitations: Runtime assertions can be disabled or too late; types may not express temporal properties.

methods.name: Bidirectional traceability and V-model reasoning
methods.summary: Map needs to requirements, design, implementation, and verification, then trace failures back to the owning premise.
methods.positive_trigger: Regulated/high-consequence work or many interacting requirement/design/test artifacts.
methods.negative_trigger: Small reversible change with a compact AC/SC/VO chain already sufficient.
steps: map each claim downstream and evidence upstream
methods.evidence: No normative claim or verification obligation is orphaned.
methods.fallback: Use a compact AC/SC/VO table.
methods.limitations: Trace completeness does not establish semantic correctness.

methods.name: Adaptive change impact and plan graph
methods.summary: Trace callers, consumers, data, errors, configuration, generated artifacts, operations, compatibility directions, and implementation dependencies; update the plan as code changes expose new edges.
methods.positive_trigger: A change crosses a public boundary or has uncertain blast radius/dependency order.
methods.negative_trigger: A proven private leaf with no callers, data, config, generated, packaging, or operational effects.
steps: trace direct callers consumers and repository-level dependency edges
follow data errors configuration generated packaging and operations
order coherent changes by dependency and protected compatibility
retrace changed nodes and replan when implementation reveals a new edge
methods.evidence: Each affected edge maps to implementation or verification and new discoveries update the plan rather than remain undocumented.
methods.fallback: Use conservative bounded search and mark unobserved dynamic/external consumers unknown.
methods.limitations: Static search and plan graphs miss reflective, dynamic, external, or runtime-only consumers; graph completeness is not proven.

methods.name: Feature interaction analysis
methods.summary: Analyze how independently valid features conflict through shared state, ordering, priority, resources, or policies.
methods.positive_trigger: Two or more features share state/resources or compose differently by order/configuration.
methods.negative_trigger: Features are demonstrably isolated by boundary and resource ownership.
methods.evidence: Counterexample combinations are resolved and tested.
methods.fallback: Start with pairwise interaction matrix and escalate hotspots.
methods.limitations: Pairwise analysis may miss higher-order interactions.

methods.name: Bounded context and context map
methods.summary: Separate models by language/ownership boundary and make translations and upstream/downstream relationships explicit.
methods.positive_trigger: The same concept has different models or ownership across subsystems.
methods.negative_trigger: A single cohesive model and owner covers the change.
methods.evidence: Cross-context examples preserve intended meaning.
methods.fallback: Keep translation at the existing boundary and document unresolved domain ownership.
methods.limitations: Boundaries chosen for organization alone may fragment a coherent model.

methods.name: ATAM-style architecture tradeoff analysis
methods.summary: Evaluate architectural approaches against prioritized quality scenarios, sensitivity points, tradeoffs, risks, and non-risks.
methods.positive_trigger: Material architecture with competing quality attributes and costly reversal.
methods.negative_trigger: A bounded reversible local design with one dominant constraint.
steps: consolidate risk themes and evidence tasks
methods.evidence: Each major tradeoff is linked to a scenario and validation plan.
methods.fallback: Use a lightweight quality-scenario/alternative table.
methods.limitations: Workshop analysis does not replace measurements or formal proof.

methods.name: Architecture fitness function
methods.summary: Encode important architecture characteristics as continuously executable checks.
methods.positive_trigger: A critical boundary or quality characteristic can silently erode over time.
methods.negative_trigger: The invariant is already fully enforced by compiler/schema/native tooling.
methods.evidence: The check fails under a targeted violating mutation.
methods.fallback: Use an explicit review checklist with owner and expiry.
methods.limitations: Poor proxies can optimize the metric while missing the quality.

methods.name: Architecture spike or executable prototype
methods.summary: Isolate a high-uncertainty technical question and produce adopt/reject evidence without silently shipping the spike.
methods.positive_trigger: A key design premise cannot be resolved cheaply by current evidence.
methods.negative_trigger: The repository already contains a proven analogue or the question is semantic/user-owned.
steps: adopt reject or reopen with limitations
methods.evidence: Reproducible experiment tied to the design decision.
methods.fallback: Choose the most reversible design and preserve the unknown.
methods.limitations: Prototype code and benchmark environments are not production proof.

methods.name: Data lineage and provenance mapping
methods.summary: Trace data origin, transformations, ownership, retention, quality, access, sinks, and deletion across boundaries.
methods.positive_trigger: Persisted/personal data crosses stores, schemas, services, or lifecycle stages.
methods.negative_trigger: Ephemeral non-sensitive local data with no boundary or persistence change.
methods.evidence: Representative records can be traced and deletion/transform invariants tested.
methods.fallback: Mark opaque external segments and block claims depending on them.
methods.limitations: Static lineage misses shadow pipelines and runtime misconfiguration.

methods.name: Information hiding and modularity analysis
methods.summary: Localize likely-to-change decisions behind stable cohesive interfaces and explicit ownership.
methods.positive_trigger: A design exposes volatile decisions or duplicates responsibility across modules.
methods.negative_trigger: The existing boundary is cohesive, stable, and directly owns the changed decision.
steps: hide volatile decisions behind minimal interface
methods.evidence: Change impact and architecture checks show localized effects.
methods.fallback: Keep the change at the current owner and avoid premature abstraction.
methods.limitations: More modules/interfaces can increase indirection without reducing change cost.

methods.name: Alloy relational modeling
methods.summary: Model identities, sets, relations, scopes, invariants, and counterexamples with bounded exhaustive analysis.
methods.positive_trigger: Relational structure, identity, permissions, or configuration interactions have subtle counterexamples within a useful bound.
methods.negative_trigger: Primarily temporal/progress behavior or a simple invariant already exhaustively covered by types/tests.
methods.evidence: Analyzer results with explicit finite scope and reviewed mapping.
methods.fallback: Use tables/graphs and property tests; mark bounded exhaustiveness NOT RUN.
methods.limitations: No counterexample within a bound is not an unbounded proof; model-to-code mapping can be wrong.

methods.name: TLA+/PlusCal temporal modeling
methods.summary: Model concurrent/distributed state transitions and check safety, liveness, fairness, ordering, and recovery properties.
methods.positive_trigger: Correctness depends on interleavings, progress, fairness, retries, leadership, or distributed recovery.
methods.negative_trigger: Sequential stateless behavior or concurrency already encapsulated by a proven primitive.
steps: check bounded instances and map traces to tests/design
methods.evidence: Model checker result plus explicit refinement mapping to implementation.
methods.fallback: Use state/sequence models and deterministic scheduler tests; mark temporal proof NOT RUN.
methods.limitations: Fairness assumptions and abstraction choices can hide real failures.

methods.name: Event-B refinement
methods.summary: Develop an abstract state/event model through proof-obligation-bearing refinements toward implementation detail.
methods.positive_trigger: High-consequence stateful behavior needs stepwise invariant-preserving refinement.
methods.negative_trigger: Routine reversible work without formal assurance need or proof expertise.
methods.evidence: Discharged proof obligations and reviewed code mapping.
methods.fallback: Use explicit invariants, state model, and refinement review.
methods.limitations: Proof covers the model and assumptions, not unspecified implementation/environment behavior.

methods.name: Refinement mapping and simulation relation
methods.summary: Show how concrete implementation states/steps correspond to an abstract specification while preserving observable behavior.
methods.positive_trigger: A new implementation, migration, optimization, or protocol must preserve a high-value abstract contract.
methods.negative_trigger: The public behavior is intentionally changing and no abstract preservation claim is made.
methods.evidence: Machine-checked or independently reviewed obligations plus conformance tests.
methods.fallback: Use differential/contract/characterization tests and state limitations.
methods.limitations: An incomplete abstraction function can prove the wrong contract.

methods.name: Petri net or process model
methods.summary: Represent concurrency, synchronization, resource tokens, reachability, deadlock, and workflow composition.
methods.positive_trigger: Workflow/resource correctness depends on concurrent enablement, synchronization, or token conservation.
methods.negative_trigger: A simple sequential state machine adequately represents behavior.
methods.evidence: Tool result and implementation mapping.
methods.fallback: Use explicit state/resource tables and scheduler tests.
methods.limitations: Time, data values, and implementation scheduling may require richer models.

methods.name: Interactive theorem proving
methods.summary: Prove high-value mathematical or program properties under explicit axioms with machine-checked proof.
methods.positive_trigger: Catastrophic failure cost and a stable formal specification justify proof investment.
methods.negative_trigger: Requirements are volatile, stakes are ordinary, or proof/code mapping cannot be maintained.
steps: review trusted base and implementation correspondence
methods.evidence: Reproducible proof check and explicit trusted assumptions.
methods.fallback: Use model checking, property testing, independent derivation, and assurance case.
methods.limitations: Proof is only as relevant as the specification, axioms, trusted base, and refinement mapping.

methods.name: STRIDE threat modeling
methods.summary: Enumerate spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service, and elevation threats across trust boundaries.
methods.positive_trigger: A security-sensitive data flow or trust boundary changes.
methods.negative_trigger: No security boundary, asset, identity, or untrusted input is affected.
steps: draw assets flows and trust boundaries
methods.evidence: Boundary-specific negative tests and control inspection.
methods.fallback: Use misuse cases and conservative boundary validation.
methods.limitations: STRIDE finds categories, not complete exploit paths or risk probability.

methods.name: Attack tree
methods.summary: Decompose an adversary goal into alternative and conjunctive attack paths, controls, assumptions, and tests.
methods.positive_trigger: A high-value asset or attacker goal needs path-oriented analysis.
methods.negative_trigger: No credible adversarial actor or asset is in scope.
methods.evidence: Controls block representative feasible paths.
methods.fallback: Use a threat/misuse checklist and record unmodeled paths.
methods.limitations: Trees can miss cross-goal interactions and unknown attacks.

methods.name: LINDDUN privacy threat modeling
methods.summary: Analyze linkability, identifiability, non-repudiation, detectability, disclosure, unawareness, and non-compliance over personal-data flows.
methods.positive_trigger: Personal/sensitive data, identity linkage, consent, retention, or disclosure changes.
methods.negative_trigger: No personal/sensitive data or privacy-relevant metadata is processed.
methods.evidence: Data-flow-specific tests and retention/access/deletion evidence.
methods.fallback: Use a privacy data inventory and conservative minimization.
methods.limitations: Does not itself determine legal compliance or user acceptability.

methods.name: NIST SSDF secure development practices
methods.summary: Integrate preparation, protection, production, and vulnerability response controls into the development lifecycle.
methods.positive_trigger: Security-relevant software or supply-chain changes.
methods.negative_trigger: No security-relevant asset/boundary/dependency and existing native controls fully cover the unchanged path.
methods.evidence: Repository-native controls plus contextual review.
methods.fallback: Apply the smallest relevant practices and record uncovered controls.
methods.limitations: A framework organizes controls; it does not prove a product secure.

methods.name: FMEA and fault-tree analysis
methods.summary: Analyze component failure modes/effects bottom-up and top-event causal combinations top-down.
methods.positive_trigger: Failure can cause material safety, data, financial, or service harm.
methods.negative_trigger: Low-consequence local failure with simple typed handling and no propagation.
methods.evidence: Fault injection or analysis closes high-priority paths.
methods.fallback: Use a bounded failure-mode checklist and keep residual risk explicit.
methods.limitations: Ordinal scores are prioritization aids, not calibrated risk probabilities.

methods.name: STPA control-structure analysis
methods.summary: Identify accidents, hazards, unsafe control actions, causal scenarios, and enforceable safety constraints in sociotechnical control loops.
methods.positive_trigger: Unsafe control actions or interactions can cause unacceptable losses even without component failure.
methods.negative_trigger: No safety hazard/control loop or consequences do not justify specialist analysis.
steps: derive causal scenarios constraints and tests
methods.evidence: Constraints trace into design, monitoring, and scenario tests.
methods.fallback: Use FMEA/FTA plus explicit control/invariant review.
methods.limitations: Quality depends heavily on system boundary and domain participation.

methods.name: HAZOP-style guideword analysis
methods.summary: Apply structured deviations such as no, more, less, reverse, early, late, and other-than to flows and operations.
methods.positive_trigger: Process/flow deviations can create consequential hazards or data loss.
methods.negative_trigger: Simple stateless behavior without consequential deviations.
methods.evidence: High-consequence deviations have prevention/detection/recovery proof.
methods.fallback: Use guidewords as an adversarial checklist and state domain limits.
methods.limitations: Guidewords support completeness but do not quantify risk.

methods.name: GSN assurance case
methods.summary: Structure consequential claims, argument strategies, context, assumptions, evidence, and defeaters.
methods.positive_trigger: A high-consequence acceptance claim needs explicit multi-source argument and residual assumptions.
methods.negative_trigger: Routine low-risk change where AC/VO traceability is sufficient.
methods.evidence: Every leaf is supported or explicitly unresolved.
methods.fallback: Use a lightweight claim-evidence-limit table.
methods.limitations: A persuasive argument can still rest on invalid evidence or assumptions.

methods.name: SLSA, SBOM, and provenance assurance
methods.summary: Inventory dependencies and bind build/source provenance, integrity levels, and verifiable release artifacts.
methods.positive_trigger: Dependencies, build pipeline, generated artifacts, or release provenance change.
methods.negative_trigger: No dependency/build/release artifact change and existing provenance remains valid.
methods.evidence: Reproducible attestations or explicit NOT RUN gaps.
methods.fallback: Pin exact inputs/hashes and document unverifiable stages.
methods.limitations: Provenance does not prove source correctness or runtime safety.

methods.name: Test-driven development
methods.summary: Use a focused failing test, minimal implementation, and refactoring cycle to shape behavior and design feedback.
methods.positive_trigger: A behavior can be expressed through a fast deterministic oracle before or with implementation.
methods.negative_trigger: The first useful evidence requires unavailable physical/external infrastructure or exploratory learning; use a spike/characterization instead.
methods.evidence: Pre-change failure and post-change pass at the target boundary.
methods.fallback: Add same-slice tests and record why red-first was impractical.
methods.limitations: TDD can optimize for an incomplete or wrong oracle.

methods.name: ATDD/BDD executable scenarios
methods.summary: Drive implementation from actor-language acceptance scenarios and observable outcomes across boundaries.
methods.positive_trigger: Cross-role or end-to-end behavior benefits from shared executable examples.
methods.negative_trigger: Internal structural change with no altered observable scenario.
methods.evidence: Scenarios fail on semantic regression and remain readable to stakeholders.
methods.fallback: Keep examples in the acceptance matrix without a BDD framework.
methods.limitations: Slow brittle end-to-end steps can obscure rather than clarify behavior.

methods.name: Typestate and smart types
methods.summary: Make invalid values or lifecycle transitions unrepresentable at compile-time where the language and boundary permit.
methods.positive_trigger: Invalid construction/transition is consequential and a stable type-level distinction exists.
methods.negative_trigger: State is runtime-dynamic/cross-process or type complexity would exceed the protected invariant.
methods.evidence: Invalid cases fail to compile or are rejected at the boundary.
methods.fallback: Use validated constructors plus explicit runtime contracts.
methods.limitations: Types cannot prove external state, temporal fairness, or semantic correctness alone.

methods.name: Parallel change and expand-contract
methods.summary: Preserve compatibility by adding the new shape, migrating consumers/data, then removing the old shape after evidence.
methods.positive_trigger: Producer/consumer or schema changes cannot be atomic and old/new versions must coexist.
methods.negative_trigger: A private atomic change with no persisted data or independent consumer.
steps: remove only after evidence and authority
methods.evidence: Contract/matrix tests cover every coexistence direction.
methods.fallback: Block incompatible cutover until coordinated migration is authorized.
methods.limitations: Long coexistence increases complexity and cleanup debt.

methods.name: Branch by abstraction and governed feature flags
methods.summary: Introduce an abstraction/flag to switch implementations safely with owner, expiry, observability, and removal conditions.
methods.positive_trigger: A large replacement needs incremental integration or controlled exposure.
methods.negative_trigger: Small atomic change or flag lifecycle cannot be owned/cleaned.
steps: remove old path/flag at explicit gate
methods.evidence: Both modes and transition/cleanup are tested.
methods.fallback: Use isolated vertical slices without a permanent toggle.
methods.limitations: Flags multiply configurations and can create hidden feature interactions.

methods.name: Strangler migration
methods.summary: Incrementally route bounded behavior from a legacy system to a new owner while preserving coexistence and rollback.
methods.positive_trigger: A monolith/legacy capability must be replaced incrementally across a stable seam.
methods.negative_trigger: No stable seam, atomic replacement is safer, or dual ownership would corrupt data.
steps: cut over and remove after reconciliation
methods.evidence: Per-slice contract/data/rollback proof.
methods.fallback: First create a stable contract or anti-corruption boundary.
methods.limitations: Dual write/read and ownership ambiguity are major failure sources.

methods.name: Cleanroom software development
methods.summary: Use precise specification, correctness reasoning/inspection, incremental development, and statistically grounded usage testing.
methods.positive_trigger: High-assurance logic has stable formalizable requirements and the team can sustain correctness verification and operational-profile testing.
methods.negative_trigger: Requirements are volatile, feedback depends on exploratory execution, or ordinary risk does not justify the ceremony.
steps: test from an operational usage distribution
methods.evidence: Inspection/proof records plus statistically interpreted test results.
methods.fallback: Use contracts, formal inspection, property tests, and representative workloads.
methods.limitations: Operational profiles and proofs can be wrong; strict process may be uneconomic.

methods.name: N-version programming
methods.summary: Build independently designed implementations and adjudicate their outputs to tolerate some design faults.
methods.positive_trigger: Consequences justify independent implementations and common-mode failure can be meaningfully reduced.
methods.negative_trigger: Shared specification/toolchain/data dominates failure or cost cannot support genuine independence.
steps: adjudicate disagreements and analyze common-mode faults
methods.evidence: Independent provenance and disagreement/fault-injection results.
methods.fallback: Use one implementation plus independent derivation/differential oracle.
methods.limitations: Versions often share correlated requirement, tool, and conceptual faults; voting can mask them.

methods.name: Formal inspection and structured pairing
methods.summary: Use assigned roles, preparation, defect logging, repair, and re-inspection for consequential code/specification.
methods.positive_trigger: Dense, unsafe, security-sensitive, generated, or high-consequence logic needs human/independent scrutiny.
methods.negative_trigger: Mechanical low-risk change fully covered by deterministic native checks.
steps: log evidence-bearing defects without solving in meeting
methods.evidence: Closed defect records and fresh checks.
methods.fallback: Use focused pair review plus checklist and oracle challenge.
methods.limitations: Meetings without preparation/roles become low-signal walkthroughs.

methods.name: Reproduction minimization
methods.summary: Reduce a failure to the smallest stable environment, input, sequence, and dependency set that preserves the symptom.
methods.positive_trigger: A defect is noisy, broad, environment-sensitive, or expensive to reproduce.
methods.negative_trigger: A focused deterministic regression already isolates the cause.
steps: verify reduced case has same causal signature
methods.evidence: Original and reduced failures share the discriminating signature.
methods.fallback: Freeze the smallest currently repeatable case and list instability.
methods.limitations: Over-minimization can remove timing/context that is part of the real cause.

methods.name: Delta debugging and bisection
methods.summary: Systematically minimize failure-inducing inputs/configurations or locate the introducing revision with controlled partitions.
methods.positive_trigger: Failure depends on a large reducible input/config/diff or a known-good/known-bad history interval.
methods.negative_trigger: Non-monotonic flaky behavior lacks a stable predicate or history is incomparable.
steps: verify minimal cause in original context
methods.evidence: Reproducible predicate and final minimal delta/revision.
methods.fallback: Use hypothesis experiments and causal graph when partition assumptions fail.
methods.limitations: Interactions and flaky predicates can invalidate binary/minimal conclusions.

methods.name: Fault injection for diagnosis
methods.summary: Inject controlled failures at suspected boundaries to distinguish propagation, handling, recovery, and observability hypotheses.
methods.positive_trigger: Failure handling/recovery path is hard to trigger naturally but can be isolated safely.
methods.negative_trigger: Injection could affect real users/data or the boundary cannot be safely controlled.
methods.evidence: Targeted logs/state/oracles discriminate causal hypotheses.
methods.fallback: Use mocks/simulation/static path inspection and keep runtime proof open.
methods.limitations: Injected faults may not reproduce timing or correlated real failures.

methods.name: Equivalence partitioning and boundary-value analysis
methods.summary: Partition inputs/states by expected behavior and test valid, invalid, edge, just-inside, and just-outside values.
methods.positive_trigger: Inputs, limits, ranges, sizes, states, or partitions affect behavior.
methods.negative_trigger: No meaningful input/state partition exists, with a concrete reason.
methods.evidence: Each class/boundary maps to an oracle.
methods.fallback: Use representative normal/error cases and state the uncovered domain.
methods.limitations: Interactions and temporal sequences need additional techniques.

methods.name: Combinatorial t-way testing
methods.summary: Cover all value combinations up to strength t for configurable multi-factor behavior.
methods.positive_trigger: Many discrete factors/options create interaction risk beyond feasible exhaustive testing.
methods.negative_trigger: Few combinations can be exhaustively tested or factors are continuous/stateful without useful discretization.
methods.evidence: Coverage checker and result per generated configuration.
methods.fallback: Use pairwise manual matrix and document higher-order gaps.
methods.limitations: Faults requiring interactions above t or invalid factor models remain uncovered.

methods.name: Property-based testing
methods.summary: Generate broad inputs to check invariants, round trips, algebraic laws, stateful properties, and shrink failures.
methods.positive_trigger: General invariants are clearer and broader than enumerated examples.
methods.negative_trigger: No valid generator/property exists or examples carry essential semantics not captured by the property.
methods.evidence: Reproducible seeds/counterexamples and failure-sensitive properties.
methods.fallback: Use table-driven boundary examples.
methods.limitations: Weak properties and biased generators create false confidence.

methods.name: Model-based testing
methods.summary: Generate action sequences and expected outcomes from an abstract state/behavior model.
methods.positive_trigger: Stateful API/workflow behavior has many sequences and a tractable abstract model.
methods.negative_trigger: Stateless/simple behavior or no independent model oracle.
methods.evidence: Model/system divergence with reproducible trace.
methods.fallback: Use hand-derived state-transition tests.
methods.limitations: Shared defects between model and implementation can hide failures.

methods.name: Metamorphic testing
methods.summary: Test relations between transformed inputs and outputs when exact expected outputs are hard to know.
methods.positive_trigger: The oracle is weak but trustworthy input/output relations exist.
methods.negative_trigger: A direct exact oracle exists and metamorphic relations add no distinct failure class.
methods.evidence: Violations localize oracle/system inconsistencies.
methods.fallback: Use differential or property tests.
methods.limitations: Incorrect relations can reject valid behavior or preserve shared defects.

methods.name: Differential testing
methods.summary: Compare independent implementations, versions, models, backends, or platforms over the same generated/curated inputs.
methods.positive_trigger: An independent executable reference or old/new implementation exists.
methods.negative_trigger: Compared implementations share the same code/path or intentionally differ without a normalization contract.
methods.evidence: Independent outputs and reviewed normalization.
methods.fallback: Use characterization plus contract/property oracles.
methods.limitations: Agreement can reflect common-mode faults; disagreement needs a trusted adjudicator.

methods.name: Characterization and golden-master testing
methods.summary: Capture existing observable behavior to protect legacy/refactor semantics before intentional changes are separated.
methods.positive_trigger: Legacy or poorly specified behavior must remain stable through refactor/migration.
methods.negative_trigger: Existing behavior is known wrong/unstable/sensitive and should not be frozen wholesale.
steps: separate protected baseline from approved changes
methods.evidence: Pre-change capture and post-change comparison with reviewed deltas.
methods.fallback: Protect only explicitly approved invariants.
methods.limitations: Golden masters can canonize bugs and produce low-signal snapshots.

methods.name: Contract and consumer-driven testing
methods.summary: Verify provider/consumer obligations independently across public interfaces and version directions.
methods.positive_trigger: Independent producers/consumers or versions rely on a public contract.
methods.negative_trigger: A private in-process boundary changes atomically with all callers and no persisted/wire data.
steps: run provider and representative consumer checks
methods.evidence: Both sides execute against exact contract versions.
methods.fallback: Use schema/static compatibility plus integration tests and mark absent consumers.
methods.limitations: Recorded consumers may not represent all external or dynamic use.

methods.name: Mutation testing
methods.summary: Introduce small syntactic behavior changes to measure whether the test suite detects them.
methods.positive_trigger: Test oracle strength is uncertain in consequential logic.
methods.negative_trigger: No suitable mutation tool, generated/noisy code dominates, or equivalent mutants overwhelm decision value.
methods.evidence: Targeted mutants are killed for the intended assertion path.
methods.fallback: Perform a few manual/local negative-control mutations.
methods.limitations: Mutation score is not a quality target and equivalent mutants distort it.

methods.name: Semantic mutation testing
methods.summary: Mutate specification/model semantics to test whether model-based properties and implementation oracles expose meaningful requirement faults.
methods.positive_trigger: A formal/executable specification is central and ordinary code mutation cannot challenge specification adequacy.
methods.negative_trigger: No stable semantic model or ordinary oracle challenges are sufficient.
methods.evidence: Meaningful semantic faults are rejected by independent properties/evidence.
methods.fallback: Manually perturb invariants/transitions and run oracle challenges.
methods.limitations: Operator quality and model-code mapping dominate conclusions.

methods.name: Coverage-guided or grammar-based fuzzing
methods.summary: Generate high-volume malformed and structured inputs to find crashes, hangs, invariant violations, and parser/state bugs.
methods.positive_trigger: Parser/protocol/FFI/untrusted input has a fast isolated harness and crisp crash/invariant oracle.
methods.negative_trigger: Unsafe to run, no bounded harness, or only slow external effects are observable.
methods.evidence: Reproducible minimized inputs and fixed regressions.
methods.fallback: Use grammar/boundary/adversarial tests.
methods.limitations: No findings within a campaign is not proof; harness reachability matters.

methods.name: Static analysis and runtime sanitizers
methods.summary: Use language-native analysis and instrumented execution to detect type, memory, undefined behavior, race, and security defects.
methods.positive_trigger: Affected language/runtime has applicable repository-native analyzers or sanitizers.
methods.negative_trigger: The tool does not support the platform/path and no qualified configuration exists.
steps: re-run after repair and record unsupported paths
methods.evidence: Exact tool/version/config/result against final bytes.
methods.fallback: Use compiler/linter plus focused invariant/resource review.
methods.limitations: Tools have blind spots, false positives, and configuration/platform gaps.

methods.name: Symbolic execution
methods.summary: Explore program paths with symbolic inputs and solver constraints to find counterexamples or prove bounded path properties.
methods.positive_trigger: Constrained pure/low-level logic has consequential path conditions and supported tooling.
methods.negative_trigger: Environment-heavy/concurrent code causes path explosion or unsupported semantics.
methods.evidence: Reproducible tool result plus concrete replay.
methods.fallback: Use property/fuzz/boundary testing.
methods.limitations: Path explosion and environment modeling can dominate; bounded result is not whole-system proof.

methods.name: Concurrency, schedule, and linearizability testing
methods.summary: Exercise controlled interleavings and check histories against atomic/ordering/progress contracts.
methods.positive_trigger: Correctness depends on interleavings, atomicity, cancellation, duplicate delivery, or progress.
methods.negative_trigger: Concurrency is absent or wholly delegated to a proven primitive without changed use.
methods.evidence: Reproducible history violating the formal/abstract contract or broad controlled pass.
methods.fallback: Use barriers/fault injection plus TLA/state reasoning.
methods.limitations: Stress alone is probabilistic; fairness/time assumptions may differ in production.

methods.name: Fault injection and chaos engineering
methods.summary: Experiment on system resilience by introducing realistic failures with steady-state, blast-radius, abort, and recovery controls.
methods.positive_trigger: Distributed/operational resilience claims need evidence under dependency, network, process, or resource failure.
methods.negative_trigger: No isolated/authorized environment, unsafe blast radius, or no observable steady state.
methods.evidence: Telemetry and state reconciliation before/during/after.
methods.fallback: Use simulation/unit fault injection and mark production resilience NOT RUN.
methods.limitations: Experiments cover chosen faults/environments and can themselves cause harm.

methods.name: Performance, load, stress, and soak testing
methods.summary: Measure latency/throughput/resources under representative, boundary, overload, and duration workloads.
methods.positive_trigger: A measurable performance/resource/scale claim or regression risk exists.
methods.negative_trigger: No changed performance path or representative workload/threshold can be defined.
steps: measure normal boundary overload and duration
methods.evidence: Repeatable measurements with versions/configuration and variance.
methods.fallback: Use microbenchmark/profile and label environment gap.
methods.limitations: Lab workloads and hardware may not represent production; averages hide tails.

methods.name: Accessibility conformance and assistive-technology testing
methods.summary: Verify semantic, keyboard, contrast, focus, text, motion, and assistive-technology behavior against applicable criteria.
methods.positive_trigger: A user-facing interface, content, input, navigation, or state changes.
methods.negative_trigger: No user-facing surface or accessibility semantics are affected.
methods.evidence: Criterion-specific results on rendered behavior.
methods.fallback: Run code/semantic review and mark physical AT checks NOT RUN.
methods.limitations: Automated tools cover only a subset; conformance does not guarantee usability.

methods.name: Moderated usability testing
methods.summary: Observe representative users attempting realistic tasks and identify comprehension, navigation, recovery, and accessibility breakdowns.
methods.positive_trigger: Material workflow/comprehension decisions remain risky after implementation/prototype.
methods.negative_trigger: No user-facing change or established flow is preserved without new uncertainty.
steps: synthesize failures and rerun critical changes
methods.evidence: Observed behavior linked to product decisions.
methods.fallback: Use expert heuristic walkthrough and label missing user evidence.
methods.limitations: Small qualitative sessions reveal problems but do not quantify prevalence.

methods.name: Compatibility matrix
methods.summary: Test supported producer/consumer, version, platform, configuration, schema, and data directions explicitly.
methods.positive_trigger: Multiple supported versions/platforms/directions coexist or compatibility is required.
methods.negative_trigger: One private atomic version with no persisted/wire/external compatibility surface.
methods.evidence: Exact version/config/environment per executed cell.
methods.fallback: Use static schema/ABI inspection and mark runtime cells NOT RUN.
methods.limitations: Sampled matrices can miss unselected combinations and real environments.

methods.name: Migration replay, reconciliation, and rollback rehearsal
methods.summary: Exercise forward migration, restart/resume, mixed versions, reconciliation, rollback/roll-forward, and cleanup on representative data.
methods.positive_trigger: Data/schema/state migration or destructive/recovery behavior changes.
methods.negative_trigger: No persisted data/state transition or migration.
methods.evidence: Counts/hashes/invariants before and after each phase.
methods.fallback: Use isolated fixtures/static scripts and mark production-scale rehearsal NOT RUN.
methods.limitations: Representative fixtures may miss production distribution, scale, locks, and operator error.

methods.name: Independent N-version derivation
methods.summary: Have genuinely separated reviewers/implementers derive expected behavior or solutions from a neutral frozen specification, then investigate disagreements before adjudication.
methods.positive_trigger: A consequential result lacks a strong single oracle and genuine independent derivation is affordable.
methods.negative_trigger: Participants share the prior solution narrative, model/context/tool lineage, or the task is low-risk/routine.
steps: freeze a neutral specification without candidate advocacy
isolate derivations and vary model context evidence or implementation lineage where feasible
investigate disagreements and common-mode agreement before choosing
methods.evidence: Independent artifacts, provenance/diversity record, and evidence-based adjudication.
methods.fallback: Use clean-context review and differential/metamorphic tests while reporting shared-common-mode risk.
methods.limitations: Common specification, training data, model family, tools, and conceptual faults remain correlated; agreement is not truth.

methods.name: Trunk-based small-batch continuous integration
methods.summary: Keep changes small, integrated, reproducibly built, and continuously checked to reduce merge and release risk.
methods.positive_trigger: Multiple contributors or frequent integration/release makes batch size and drift consequential.
methods.negative_trigger: Read-only/local work with no authorized integration action.
methods.evidence: Fresh CI/native checks on integrated bytes.
methods.fallback: Use short-lived bounded branches and regular reconciliation.
methods.limitations: Fast integration does not replace architecture, testing, or release controls.

methods.name: Canary and progressive delivery
methods.summary: Expose a change to increasing cohorts while comparing health and aborting automatically on meaningful degradation.
methods.positive_trigger: An authorized deployment has meaningful blast radius and cohorting/telemetry/rollback controls.
methods.negative_trigger: No deployment authority, no safe cohorts, or no sensitive comparison oracle.
methods.evidence: Stage-specific telemetry and decision log.
methods.fallback: Use pre-production/shadow validation and mark live canary NOT RUN.
methods.limitations: Low traffic, noisy metrics, and delayed harms can defeat canary detection.

methods.name: Blue-green deployment and shadow traffic
methods.summary: Run old/new environments or mirror traffic to compare behavior before switching user-visible ownership.
methods.positive_trigger: Infrastructure supports parallel environments or safe read-only traffic mirroring and cutover risk is material.
methods.negative_trigger: Stateful side effects cannot be isolated or duplicate traffic would harm users/data.
steps: mirror or route bounded traffic safely
methods.evidence: Environment parity and comparison/cutover logs.
methods.fallback: Use offline replay or canary with explicit limits.
methods.limitations: State, caches, data drift, and hidden side effects make parity difficult.

methods.name: SLO and error-budget reasoning
methods.summary: Define user-centered reliability objectives, indicators, windows, and policies that balance reliability work and change velocity.
methods.positive_trigger: A running service has user-visible reliability/latency expectations and operational ownership.
methods.negative_trigger: No service/operational surface or no meaningful user-centered indicator.
methods.evidence: Measured indicators and policy decisions over the declared window.
methods.fallback: Use provisional service thresholds and label calibration pending.
methods.limitations: Targets can be gamed or detached from user harm; historical data may be sparse.

methods.name: Runbook and game-day rehearsal
methods.summary: Make operational detection, diagnosis, containment, recovery, escalation, and communication executable under realistic drills.
methods.positive_trigger: Material incidents require coordinated operational action or recovery is unproven.
methods.negative_trigger: No operational service/on-call/recovery surface.
steps: repair runbook/system and rerun critical gaps
methods.evidence: Timed drill artifacts and restored invariants.
methods.fallback: Tabletop exercise with explicit physical gaps.
methods.limitations: Rehearsed scenarios do not cover all incidents and drills can disrupt systems.

methods.name: Blameless postmortem and systems causal analysis
methods.summary: Reconstruct conditions, decisions, controls, interactions, and latent weaknesses without reducing failure to individual blame.
methods.positive_trigger: A material incident, near miss, or repeated failure produced learning worth institutionalizing.
methods.negative_trigger: No incident evidence or the exercise would be speculative blame allocation.
methods.evidence: Actions map to observed contributors and later verification.
methods.fallback: Use a concise incident review with uncertainties explicit.
methods.limitations: Retrospective narratives are vulnerable to hindsight bias and incomplete telemetry.

methods.name: Repository legibility and context engineering
methods.summary: Place durable intent, current truth, commands, invariants, and progressive references where an agent can retrieve the smallest decision-relevant context at the right time.
methods.positive_trigger: AI agents perform multi-step repository work, repeatedly miss hidden knowledge, or face a constrained context budget.
methods.negative_trigger: One-shot conceptual response with no persistent repository task.
steps: identify decisions agents cannot infer and rank context by decision value
place concise durable current truth and explicit freshness/invalidation rules
retrieve detailed references just in time instead of copying the corpus
test discovery retrieval stale-link and overload behavior
methods.evidence: Agent-visible repository paths, bounded context projections, and deterministic retrieval/staleness contract cases.
methods.fallback: Use a bounded task brief/checkpoint and fresh repository observation for the current run.
methods.limitations: More context can reduce signal; summaries lose detail; documentation can drift from code or crowd out current observations.

methods.name: Deterministic agent harness and agent-computer interface
methods.summary: Move repeatable discovery, validation, isolation, and policy checks into executable tools whose compact interface makes correct actions easy and unsafe or ambiguous actions explicit.
methods.positive_trigger: Agents repeatedly perform structured actions where deterministic feedback, interface ergonomics, or policy prevents omission.
methods.negative_trigger: A one-off judgment cannot be safely encoded or tool automation would widen authority.
steps: minimize action/observation ambiguity in the agent-computer interface
define inputs outputs errors authority idempotency and containment
mutation-test invariants forbidden actions and fallbacks
methods.evidence: Stable machine-readable outputs, efficient task-relevant observations, and forbidden-action tests.
methods.fallback: Use an explicit checklist/artifact and manual verification.
methods.limitations: Tools can enforce only modeled surfaces; a poor interface can induce agent error even when the underlying capability is correct.

methods.name: Agent evaluation and acceptance design
methods.summary: Define task-realistic outcome, trajectory, authority, side-effect, recovery, and resource oracles plus first-attempt and optional model judging without replacing repository evidence.
methods.positive_trigger: An AI workflow/Skill/prompt/tool behavior needs repeatable acceptance beyond Markdown syntax or final-state success.
methods.negative_trigger: Ordinary code behavior is already fully covered by native deterministic tests and no model/process behavior claim exists.
steps: define real outcomes forbidden actions side effects recovery and cost/resource observations
prefer deterministic state and trace graders
separate executor grader and infrastructure artifacts
measure first attempts inspect case health and report component results without a composite proxy
methods.evidence: Versioned case/trajectory/results with exact model/tool/repository/environment identity, typed infrastructure outcomes, and limitations.
methods.fallback: Use deterministic outcome and forbidden-action contracts only and mark live model/trajectory behavior NOT RUN.
methods.limitations: Benchmarks can be contaminated, saturated, noisy, unrepresentative, or gamed; final state can hide unsafe process.

methods.name: Multiple independent first attempts
methods.summary: Use predeclared paired/randomized repeated first attempts to expose decision-relevant variance and common failures without iterative contamination.
methods.positive_trigger: Stochastic agent behavior and consequence justify estimating variance or comparing strategies across representative cases.
methods.negative_trigger: Deterministic code tests answer the question or sample/budget/independence cannot support the intended decision.
steps: freeze estimand cases pairing/randomization unit of analysis stopping/retry rules and identities
run isolated first attempts without repair feedback while preserving typed infrastructure failures
grade with stable outcome trajectory and safety oracles
report effect variability intervals where justified case heterogeneity and qualitative failures
methods.evidence: Raw per-attempt artifacts, pairing/randomization record, infrastructure-error accounting, stopping rule, and aggregation method.
methods.fallback: Run one clearly labeled first attempt plus deterministic contracts and make no population/comparative claim.
methods.limitations: Small convenience samples, repeated trials on the same cases, mutable models, and infrastructure noise create wide or biased uncertainty; attempt count is not quality.

methods.name: Model and tool identity pinning
methods.summary: Bind evaluation and execution claims to exact model, tool, Skill, prompt, repository, configuration, and environment identities.
methods.positive_trigger: A claim depends on a hosted model, mutable tool, Skill, prompt, or runtime.
methods.negative_trigger: Pure deterministic local behavior with exact repository/tool version already captured.
methods.evidence: Machine-readable identity and source digests.
methods.fallback: State the unresolved identity and avoid comparative/current claims.
methods.limitations: Provider internals and mutable aliases may remain opaque.

methods.name: Evaluation contamination and case-health analysis
methods.summary: Check benchmark freshness, ambiguity, broken environments, saturation, memorization risk, grader validity, and task representativeness.
methods.positive_trigger: Agent benchmark/eval results influence product or quality decisions.
methods.negative_trigger: No model evaluation or benchmark claim is made.
steps: separate score from qualitative failure evidence
methods.evidence: Case-level audit and reproducible grader checks.
methods.fallback: Treat results as exploratory and rely on repository-native evidence.
methods.limitations: Contamination is difficult to prove absent and benchmark validity changes over time.

methods.name: Agent authority and tool-boundary modeling
methods.summary: Separate requested outcome from mutation, dependency, destructive, external, secret, and delivery authorities; bind tools to least privilege and stop conditions.
methods.positive_trigger: An agent can mutate repositories, data, infrastructure, accounts, or external communication.
methods.negative_trigger: Read-only conceptual work with no tool or external action.
steps: stop and request on boundary expansion
methods.evidence: Forbidden-action tests and durable approval records.
methods.fallback: Restrict to read-only/local reversible actions.
methods.limitations: Prompt policy is not a complete security boundary; host/tool enforcement matters.

methods.name: Long-running semantic checkpoint and action ledger
methods.summary: Persist digest-bound semantic state plus an append-only ledger of attempted actions, side effects, idempotency keys, compensation, and unresolved work.
methods.positive_trigger: Work spans slices, interruptions, compaction, delegation, premise changes, verification handoff, or consequential external actions.
methods.negative_trigger: Single-turn non-mutating micro work with no continuity or side-effect risk.
steps: record attempted actions outcomes side effects idempotency and compensation
reconcile drift and outstanding work before resume/final claims
methods.evidence: Checkpoint validates against current bytes and every consequential action has a terminal or explicitly outstanding ledger state.
methods.fallback: Write a concise recovery note, inventory possible side effects, and re-discover before resuming.
methods.limitations: A checkpoint is an unsigned consistency record, not tamper-proof history or a distributed transaction log.

methods.name: Minimum-effective autonomy
methods.summary: Choose the least autonomous pattern that satisfies the task, escalating from deterministic workflow to model-directed agent only when adaptivity pays for its added uncertainty.
methods.positive_trigger: A system or task owner must choose between script, workflow, single agent, evaluator loop, or multi-agent execution.
methods.negative_trigger: The autonomy shape is fixed by an approved external contract and no safety or cost concern is present.
steps: start with the least autonomous viable pattern
add tools loops or agents only for observed uncertainty
bind escalation stop and human-control conditions
methods.evidence: A simpler alternative is compared against the selected autonomy with explicit failure/cost tradeoffs.
methods.fallback: Use a deterministic workflow with explicit human decisions.
methods.limitations: Low autonomy can underperform in open-ended environments; the decision must be revisited when task variability changes.

methods.name: Belief-state and active information acquisition
methods.summary: Represent known, unknown, stale, conflicting, and confidence-qualified facts, then choose the cheapest observation that best discriminates the next material decision.
methods.positive_trigger: The agent acts from incomplete, stale, contradictory, or probabilistic observations and another inspection can change the decision.
methods.negative_trigger: All decision-critical facts are deterministic, current, and directly observed.
steps: separate observation inference unknown and staleness
rank safe observations by discrimination cost and freshness
update beliefs and invalidate dependent plans
methods.evidence: The chosen observation rejects alternatives or narrows an explicit uncertainty that affects action.
methods.fallback: Use the conservative reversible action and mark the unresolved belief.
methods.limitations: Subjective confidence is not calibrated probability and information gain estimates can be wrong.

methods.name: Receding-horizon execution
methods.summary: Plan deeply enough to protect dependencies and invariants, execute one bounded horizon, observe real state, and replan instead of committing to a stale open-loop script.
methods.positive_trigger: A long task runs in a changing repository, service, tool, or external environment where later steps depend on fresh outcomes.
methods.negative_trigger: A short deterministic transaction can execute atomically against a stable snapshot.
steps: map non-negotiable dependencies and end state
plan the next reversible bounded horizon
reconcile drift and replan before expanding
methods.evidence: Every horizon binds preconditions, executed effects, fresh observations, and the reason the next plan remains valid.
methods.fallback: Stop at the last verified checkpoint and rediscover current state.
methods.limitations: Frequent replanning adds cost and can become myopic without a stable end-state contract.

methods.name: Counterexample-guided repair
methods.summary: Iterate candidate repair, independent counterexample generation, and constraint refinement until the repair satisfies the bounded specification or exposes an unresolved oracle gap.
methods.positive_trigger: An automated or AI-generated repair repeatedly fits visible examples while plausible counterexamples remain.
methods.negative_trigger: The causal defect and complete regression oracle are already deterministic and the first minimal repair passes them.
steps: freeze protected semantics and seed oracle
search independently for a distinguishing counterexample
add valid counterexamples and repeat without weakening the oracle
methods.evidence: Each rejected candidate has a replayable counterexample and the accepted candidate passes the accumulated corpus plus native regression gates.
methods.fallback: Return to hypothesis-led debugging and keep patch-overfit risk open.
methods.limitations: The loop converges only within the expressiveness of its generator and oracle; it cannot prove absence of unseen defects.

methods.name: Runtime assurance and safety shield
methods.summary: Place a simple independently enforceable safety monitor and verified fallback around a capable but untrusted agent/controller.
methods.positive_trigger: An adaptive agent can issue consequential actions whose safety cannot be fully established before execution.
methods.negative_trigger: All outputs are advisory or the complete action space is already deterministically validated before effect.
steps: define prohibited states and action envelope
switch to a bounded safe fallback on violation or uncertainty
methods.evidence: Unsafe candidate actions are blocked before effect and fallback behavior is exercised under boundary faults.
methods.fallback: Remove execution authority and require human approval for each consequential action.
methods.limitations: A shield protects only encoded hazards and can itself fail; independent enforcement and fail-safe defaults are essential.

methods.name: Temporal runtime verification
methods.summary: Monitor event traces against executable safety, ordering, response-time, retry, and progress properties while the agent or workflow runs.
methods.positive_trigger: Correctness depends on event sequence, deadlines, eventual response, bounded retries, or forbidden action ordering at runtime.
methods.negative_trigger: A pure deterministic function has no temporal protocol or runtime interaction.
steps: translate requirements into observable temporal properties
define event identity clocks and incomplete-trace semantics
monitor normal fault retry and cancellation traces
bind violations to stop compensation or escalation
methods.evidence: Recorded traces demonstrate both accepting and deliberately violating monitor paths.
methods.fallback: Use offline trace checking and mark live monitoring NOT RUN.
methods.limitations: Runtime verification sees only instrumented events and observed executions; liveness on finite traces needs explicit semantics.

methods.name: Saga and compensating actions
methods.summary: Decompose a multi-step external operation into idempotent local actions with persisted progress, explicit compensations, retry rules, and reconciliation.
methods.positive_trigger: An agent or workflow performs multiple externally visible steps that cannot share one atomic transaction.
methods.negative_trigger: The operation is read-only or one bounded atomic transaction with reliable rollback.
steps: enumerate local transactions and durable progress
define idempotency retry timeout and cancellation semantics
design semantic compensation for each committed step
test interruption duplicate delivery compensation failure and reconciliation
methods.evidence: Replayable histories show no silent duplicate effect and every partial state has an owned recovery disposition.
methods.fallback: Reduce to one human-confirmed step at a time and reconcile after each effect.
methods.limitations: Compensation is not rollback: external observations and irreversible effects may remain.

methods.name: Agent trajectory and intervention evaluation
methods.summary: Evaluate not only final state but also the action trajectory, side effects, recovery behavior, and controlled interventions that distinguish causal failure mechanisms.
methods.positive_trigger: An agent can reach a superficially correct result through unsafe, wasteful, unauthorized, brittle, or unrecoverable behavior.
methods.negative_trigger: A deterministic one-step output has no meaningful action trajectory or side effect.
steps: define outcome trajectory authority and recovery oracles separately
capture actions observations tool errors and state deltas
intervene on prompt context tool environment and model factors one at a time
compare causal signatures and preserve first attempts
methods.evidence: Replayable traces and controlled interventions distinguish at least the material competing failure explanations.
methods.fallback: Use deterministic outcome and forbidden-action contracts while marking trajectory causality NOT RUN.
methods.limitations: Logged traces may omit hidden model state and interventions can change the task distribution.

methods.name: Instruction and data provenance taint tracking
methods.summary: Track the origin, trust level, transformations, and permitted influence of instructions and retrieved data before they can select tools or authorize effects.
methods.positive_trigger: An agent consumes web, email, documents, tool output, memory, or user-controlled content that can influence consequential actions.
methods.negative_trigger: All instructions and data are local trusted constants and the agent has no mutation or disclosure capability.
steps: define precedence declassification and forbidden influence
propagate provenance through retrieval memory and tool results
test indirect injection exfiltration and confused-deputy paths
methods.evidence: Untrusted content cannot silently cross into privileged instruction, secret, or external-action sinks.
methods.fallback: Treat all retrieved content as data, disable consequential tools, and require trusted human confirmation.
methods.limitations: Natural-language taint is approximate; host isolation and least privilege remain necessary.

methods.name: Human-agent function allocation
methods.summary: Allocate sensing, judgment, execution, monitoring, exception handling, and accountability between humans, deterministic controls, and agents according to capability and consequence.
methods.positive_trigger: A product or workflow needs a defensible division of decision and action rights between people and AI.
methods.negative_trigger: The system is fully deterministic with no human-AI handoff or consequential judgment.
steps: decompose sensing judgment action monitoring and recovery functions
compare human agent and deterministic-control strengths and failure modes
assign authority confidence thresholds and handoffs
test override timing workload mode confusion and failure recovery
methods.evidence: Representative scenarios show the assigned actor receives sufficient context time and control to detect and recover from failures.
methods.fallback: Keep consequential judgment and action with the human while the agent remains advisory.
methods.limitations: Human-in-the-loop is not automatically safe; overload, automation bias, latency, and unclear accountability can worsen outcomes.

methods.name: Agent memory lifecycle governance
methods.summary: Govern what agent memory may store, who it belongs to, how it is validated, scoped, updated, expired, corrected, audited, and deleted.
methods.positive_trigger: An agent persists facts, preferences, summaries, tool results, plans, or embeddings across turns, tasks, users, or repositories.
methods.negative_trigger: All context is ephemeral within one isolated non-sensitive execution.
steps: inventory stores identities sources readers and writers
define admission provenance scope retention correction and deletion
validate memory before use and invalidate on drift
test cross-user leakage poisoning replay staleness and deletion
methods.evidence: Every persisted item has owner provenance scope lifecycle and a tested invalidation/deletion path.
methods.fallback: Disable persistent memory and rebuild context from authoritative current sources.
methods.limitations: Summaries lose detail and embeddings obscure provenance; deletion from derived indexes may require separate proof.

methods.name: Multi-agent topology and ownership design
methods.summary: Choose single-agent, manager-worker, parallel independent, debate, or pipeline topology from task dependency and coordination cost, with exclusive ownership and root adjudication.
methods.positive_trigger: Multiple agents are proposed for decomposable work and coordination structure can affect quality, latency, or conflicts.
methods.negative_trigger: The task is small, tightly sequential, shares one mutable surface, or requires one coherent context.
steps: map dependency communication and shared-state edges
assign exclusive scopes interfaces deadlines and resource leases
reconcile outputs at the root and verify integration independently
methods.evidence: The chosen topology reduces a named bottleneck without unresolved ownership conflicts or dropped dependencies.
methods.fallback: Use one agent with sequential bounded slices.
methods.limitations: More agents can amplify common-mode errors and communication cost; parallelism is not quality by itself.

methods.name: Hierarchical task network planning
methods.summary: Encode reusable domain methods that decompose abstract goals into ordered primitive actions with explicit applicability constraints.
methods.positive_trigger: A stable expert domain has recurring hierarchical tasks whose legal decompositions and ordering matter.
methods.negative_trigger: The domain is novel, underspecified, rapidly changing, or ordinary dependency planning is sufficient.
steps: encode method preconditions decompositions and ordering
search and validate plans against state invariants
replay failures and maintain domain methods
