methods.evidence: Generated plans are traceable to applicable methods and pass domain-state and ordering checks.
methods.fallback: Use a dependency graph and receding-horizon plan without claiming domain completeness.
methods.limitations: Knowledge engineering is expensive and incomplete methods can exclude valid plans or admit unsafe ones.

methods.name: Behavior-tree reactive execution
methods.summary: Represent reactive control as composable conditions, actions, sequences, fallbacks, decorators, and explicit running/success/failure semantics.
methods.positive_trigger: An agent must repeatedly react to changing conditions with inspectable fallback and recovery behavior.
methods.negative_trigger: A fixed acyclic workflow or single request-response path is clearer and sufficient.
steps: define observable conditions actions and status semantics
compose sequence fallback and guard nodes
specify cancellation timeout memory and retry behavior
simulate normal changing and failing environments
methods.evidence: Tick traces expose which condition/action caused each transition and recovery path.
methods.fallback: Use an explicit state machine or workflow graph.
methods.limitations: Large trees can hide global invariants, parallel-node races, and emergent loops without separate analysis.

methods.name: Conformal risk control and selective action
methods.summary: Calibrate prediction sets, abstention, or action thresholds to a predeclared empirical risk target under stated exchangeability assumptions.
methods.positive_trigger: A stochastic model decision needs a measurable abstention/risk tradeoff and representative held-out calibration data exists.
methods.negative_trigger: No stable target loss, calibration sample, or distributional assumption can be defended.
steps: freeze exchangeable calibration and evaluation splits
compute threshold/prediction set with finite-sample procedure
test realized risk coverage abstention and distribution drift
methods.evidence: Held-out results report sample size assumptions uncertainty coverage/selectivity and failures without tuning on acceptance data.
methods.fallback: Use conservative abstention and ordinary calibrated validation without a formal coverage claim.
methods.limitations: Coverage can fail under distribution shift, dependent samples, adaptive reuse, or misspecified loss.

methods.name: Digital-twin agent simulation
methods.summary: Exercise agent policies and failure recovery against a validated, instrumented model of the environment before scarce, unsafe, or irreversible live action.
methods.positive_trigger: Live trials are unsafe, expensive, scarce, or unauthorized and a decision-useful environment model can be built.
methods.negative_trigger: A cheap isolated real environment exists or the model cannot represent the relevant failure physics/protocol.
steps: define decisions the twin must support
validate model boundaries against known real observations
run nominal boundary adversarial and fault scenarios
track reality gaps and require live confirmation before live claims
methods.evidence: Scenario results are bound to model version and validated dimensions; unsupported real-world behavior remains NOT RUN.
methods.fallback: Use isolated mocks/replay and keep live/simulation-fidelity claims open.
methods.limitations: A twin can systematically omit the exact hazards it is meant to reveal and never substitutes for authorized real-world acceptance.

methods.name: Contract-net task allocation
methods.summary: Allocate dynamic distributed tasks through announced requirements, capability/cost bids, explicit awards, progress contracts, and reassignment.
methods.positive_trigger: Heterogeneous agents or services must allocate changing tasks using local capability/cost information and centralized static scheduling is inadequate.
methods.negative_trigger: A static dependency graph and deterministic owner assignment are sufficient.
steps: define task requirements capability evidence and utility
specify announce bid award reject and completion states
handle duplicate bids timeout failure cancellation and reassignment
simulate load strategic bids partial failure and integration
methods.evidence: Protocol traces preserve single ownership, bounded allocation latency, capability constraints, and recovery under failed contractors.
methods.fallback: Use root-assigned exclusive ownership from the task dependency graph.
methods.limitations: Bidding overhead, misleading self-assessment, collusion, starvation, and integration cost can dominate the benefit.

methods.name: Architecture viewpoint consistency
methods.summary: Describe stakeholder concerns through explicit viewpoints and reconcile cross-view elements, relations, decisions, and contradictions before approval.
methods.positive_trigger: Multiple architecture views describe the same system and a decision can be locally valid while contradicting another stakeholder concern or boundary.
methods.negative_trigger: One small component has a single coherent view and no cross-view relation or stakeholder concern.
steps: map shared elements and relations across views
bind each disposition to a decision owner and verification obligation
methods.evidence: Every material concern is represented and each cross-view contradiction is resolved, deferred with authority, or kept blocking.
methods.fallback: Use one decision record with an explicit concerns and contradictions section.
methods.limitations: View consistency does not establish runtime correctness and can miss concerns omitted by stakeholders.

methods.name: Architecture reflexion and conformance
methods.summary: Map source elements to an intended architecture and classify convergences, divergences, and absences so implementation drift becomes reviewable evidence.
methods.positive_trigger: A material implementation claims an intended module or dependency architecture and drift can hide in actual source relations.
methods.negative_trigger: No intended architecture or meaningful source-to-architecture mapping exists.
steps: map concrete source elements to architecture elements
classify and disposition convergence divergence and absence
methods.evidence: Each reported relation is reproducible from source and every material divergence has a verified repair or explicit design revision.
methods.fallback: Use a bounded change-impact graph and manual dependency review.
methods.limitations: Mapping quality controls result quality; dynamic/runtime coupling may not appear in static source relations.

methods.name: BPMN collaboration and process model
methods.summary: Model participants, messages, events, gateways, timers, errors, compensation, and end states for cross-owner business workflows.
methods.positive_trigger: A business process crosses participants or systems and correctness depends on messages, timers, exceptions, compensation, or completion semantics.
methods.negative_trigger: A local acyclic function or simple state machine expresses the behavior more directly.
steps: identify participants start/end events and business outcomes
model message flows gateways timers and correlation
add error cancellation compensation and retry paths
walk representative and adversarial token traces into tests
methods.evidence: Token/message traces cover nominal, timeout, duplicate, cancellation, compensation, and terminal-state behavior without hidden ownership gaps.
methods.fallback: Use a state-transition model plus a participant/message table.
methods.limitations: BPMN can become decorative if execution semantics, data correlation, and code ownership are not mapped.

methods.name: Data quality scenarios and reconciliation
methods.summary: Turn data-quality characteristics into source-specific scenarios, measurable invariants, reconciliation rules, and owned exception handling.
methods.positive_trigger: Business correctness depends on accuracy, completeness, consistency, credibility, currentness, uniqueness, or traceable reconciliation across data sources.
methods.negative_trigger: Data is ephemeral, single-source, and already protected by a complete local type/constraint contract.
steps: identify critical data entities sources consumers and quality characteristics
define source-of-truth matching tolerance and exception rules
replay representative defects and reconcile before/after results
methods.evidence: Known bad, missing, stale, duplicate, and conflicting records exercise measurable detection and an owned reconciliation disposition.
methods.fallback: Use data lineage plus explicit field invariants and keep unmeasured characteristics open.
methods.limitations: Thresholds are domain decisions; generic quality labels cannot establish business acceptability.

methods.name: Cost-benefit architecture analysis
methods.summary: Compare architecture strategies by stakeholder-valued quality benefit, uncertainty, implementation cost, and schedule instead of optimizing technical elegance alone.
methods.positive_trigger: Finite budget or schedule must choose among credible architecture strategies with materially different quality benefits and costs.
methods.negative_trigger: There is one feasible design, no credible estimates, or the decision is cheap and reversible.
steps: estimate strategy response benefit cost schedule and uncertainty
compare incremental value and sensitivity without hiding assumptions
select a bounded strategy and define recheck thresholds
methods.evidence: The recommendation remains traceable to scenarios, estimates, uncertainty ranges, and named facts that would reverse it.
methods.fallback: Use qualitative ATAM tradeoffs and record cost evidence as unresolved.
methods.limitations: Weak estimates create false precision; the method supports a decision but does not determine stakeholder value.

methods.name: Cross-language ABI and ownership contract
methods.summary: Specify and verify representation, calling convention, ownership, errors, callbacks, threading, cancellation, teardown, and consumer packaging on both sides of an FFI boundary.
methods.positive_trigger: Code, generated bindings, or packaged binaries cross a language/runtime ABI boundary whose local success cannot prove the consumer contract.
methods.negative_trigger: The boundary is language-internal or uses a fully repository-native typed interface with no foreign ABI.
steps: inventory exported/imported symbols types layouts and calling conventions
define allocation ownership errors panics/exceptions callbacks threading cancellation and teardown
bind versioning generation linkage and packaging directions
build or contract-check both producer and representative consumers including negative paths
methods.evidence: Both sides observe the same symbol/layout/lifecycle contract and deliberate mismatch or ownership faults fail the relevant build, contract, or runtime check.
methods.fallback: Keep the boundary unchanged, inspect generated/native declarations on both sides, and mark unbuilt consumers NOT RUN.
methods.limitations: Static declarations cannot prove every runtime, loader, optimizer, architecture, or packaging combination.

risk_models.name: Cross-language ABI and FFI boundary
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Producer and consumer compile independently while disagreeing on symbols, representation, calling convention, ownership, errors, callbacks, threading, teardown, or packaging.
evidence_obligations: Both sides bind symbol, layout, lifecycle, error, threading, and packaging directions.
Unbuilt consumer, device, architecture, or packaging combinations remain NOT RUN.
risk_models.escalation: Architecture owns the boundary contract; qualified FFI review and representative consumer builds remain required where repository policy applies.

risk_models.name: Architecture views contradict stakeholder concerns
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Individually plausible architecture views encode incompatible boundaries, relations, states, or quality assumptions.
evidence_obligations: Stakeholders, concerns, viewpoints, correspondences, and contradictions are explicit.
Every material contradiction is resolved, authorized for deferral, or blocking.
risk_models.escalation: Reopen the owning architecture decision when a contradiction changes scope, contract, state, or quality obligations.

risk_models.name: Implementation drifts from intended architecture
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Actual source dependencies and ownership diverge from the approved architecture while local tests still pass.
evidence_obligations: The intended relations and source mapping are frozen before comparison.
Convergences, divergences, and absences have reproducible source evidence and disposition.
risk_models.escalation: Treat material divergence as a design defect or an explicit architecture revision, never an undocumented exception.

risk_models.name: Cross-participant workflow and message semantics
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: A business workflow passes happy-path service tests but loses message correlation, timer, cancellation, compensation, or terminal-state semantics across participants.
evidence_obligations: Participants, messages, correlation, events, gateways, errors, compensation, and end states are explicit.
Representative token/message traces map to failure-sensitive tests.
risk_models.escalation: Use formal process analysis only when concurrency/deadlock consequence and stable semantics justify it.

risk_models.name: Data quality and reconciliation failure
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Schema-valid data remains inaccurate, incomplete, stale, duplicated, contradictory, or unreconciled for the business decision it supports.
evidence_obligations: Quality characteristics, source of truth, thresholds, matching, and exception ownership are explicit.
Known bad and conflicting records demonstrate detection and reconciliation.
risk_models.escalation: Domain owners decide acceptable quality thresholds; technical checks cannot invent business truth.

risk_models.name: Architecture investment choice under finite resources
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: A costly architecture strategy is selected from technical preference without comparing stakeholder-valued benefit, uncertainty, cost, or schedule.
evidence_obligations: Credible alternatives, valued scenarios, costs, schedule, uncertainty, and reversal facts are explicit.
False numerical precision is challenged with sensitivity ranges.
risk_models.escalation: Return stakeholder value or budget decisions to the authorized owner; method output is decision support, not funding authority.

risk_models.name: Ambiguous or example-sensitive semantics
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: The implementation can be internally correct yet implement the wrong actor, rule, state, or edge-case meaning.
evidence_obligations: Competing interpretations are resolved or bounded.
Examples distinguish plausible wrong behavior.
risk_models.escalation: Escalate to user-owned clarification or product-ux-discovery when repository evidence cannot choose meaning.

risk_models.name: Identity, ontology, and cross-boundary equivalence
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Different entities are merged, the same entity is duplicated, or identity continuity is lost across time/boundaries.
evidence_obligations: Equality, alias, lifecycle, and provenance rules are explicit.
Counterexamples and migration identities are tested.
risk_models.escalation: Use Alloy/formal depth when relational counterexamples are high-consequence or configuration space is large.

risk_models.name: Feature and configuration interaction
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Individually correct features conflict through order, shared state, priority, policy, or resource composition.
evidence_obligations: Composition and precedence semantics are explicit.
Pairwise/t-way and known higher-order hotspots are exercised.
risk_models.escalation: Use process/formal modeling only for consequential concurrent or resource-token interactions.

risk_models.name: Temporal progress, fairness, and concurrency
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Safety holds in simple runs but an interleaving, retry, cancellation, starvation, or recovery trace violates progress/order/atomicity.
evidence_obligations: Safety and progress assumptions are separate.
Counterexample histories map to implementation tests.
risk_models.escalation: Use TLA+/formal depth when correctness depends on unbounded interleavings, fairness, or distributed recovery.

risk_models.name: Large relational or state space
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Examples cover happy paths while a reachable relation/state combination violates invariants.
evidence_obligations: The abstract state/input domain and bounds are explicit.
Counterexamples are replayed concretely.
risk_models.escalation: Choose relational, temporal, or symbolic form based on the actual failure mechanism, never generic complexity alone.

risk_models.name: Behavior preservation and refinement
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: A replacement appears compatible on examples but violates an abstract observation, exceptional path, or version direction.
evidence_obligations: Protected observations and intentional deltas are separate.
Every coexistence direction and exceptional behavior is accounted.
risk_models.escalation: Use formal refinement only for stable high-value contracts with proof expertise; otherwise combine contract, differential, and characterization evidence.

risk_models.name: Security trust boundary and adversarial input
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: An attacker crosses identity, trust, parser, memory, privilege, or resource boundaries not exercised by normal tests.
evidence_obligations: Assets, actors, trust boundaries, and misuse are explicit.
Controls have boundary-specific negative evidence.
risk_models.escalation: Route company-data-security and qualified specialists; do not invent cryptography or treat a scanner as complete assurance.

risk_models.name: Privacy, lineage, and identity linkage
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Data is linkable, identifiable, retained, disclosed, or deleted differently from user/system intent across an opaque flow.
evidence_obligations: Personal-data sources, transformations, sinks, retention, access, and deletion are traceable.
Privacy harms and missing legal/domain decisions remain explicit.
risk_models.escalation: Require privacy/security owner review; method output is not legal compliance advice.

risk_models.name: Safety hazard and control loss
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Unsafe control interactions or combinations cause unacceptable loss even when individual components satisfy local requirements.
evidence_obligations: Losses, hazards, constraints, controls, and assumptions are explicit.
Safety claims have independent evidence and unresolved defeaters.
risk_models.escalation: Formal/specialist methods require domain safety expertise and do not substitute for regulated approval.

risk_models.name: Weak or absent test oracle
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Tests execute code but cannot distinguish the intended result from a plausible defect.
evidence_obligations: At least one oracle is demonstrably sensitive to the target defect.
Shared assumptions and missing executable references are disclosed.
risk_models.escalation: Use semantic mutation or independent derivation only when ordinary negative controls cannot challenge a consequential oracle.

risk_models.name: Data/schema migration and coexistence
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Forward/retry/mixed-version/rollback behavior loses identity, data, order, or cleanup while happy-path migration passes.
evidence_obligations: Forward, restart, coexistence, reconciliation, rollback/roll-forward, and cleanup are explicit.
Representative data invariants are measured before and after.
risk_models.escalation: Block cutover without executable recovery and data reconciliation evidence.

risk_models.name: Performance and resource saturation
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: A design meets functional tests but violates latency, throughput, capacity, memory, or backpressure under representative load or duration.
evidence_obligations: Workload, environment, threshold, variance, and resource observations are explicit.
Optimization is tied to measured bottlenecks and portable behavior.
risk_models.escalation: Do not optimize from static intuition; keep production equivalence and soak gaps explicit.

risk_models.name: User workflow and accessibility risk
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: The implementation is technically correct but users cannot understand, navigate, recover, or use it with relevant assistive technology.
evidence_obligations: User tasks/states and accessibility criteria are explicit.
Rendered/user evidence is separated from code inference.
risk_models.escalation: Material product direction remains user-owned and requires UX Ready; absent real-user/device evidence stays NOT RUN.

risk_models.name: Rollout and operational resilience
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: A valid build causes user harm because rollout, observation, abort, rollback, or operational response is unproven.
evidence_obligations: Authority, target, health signals, thresholds, recovery, and ownership are explicit.
Unrun live/production gates cannot be reported passed.
risk_models.escalation: Delivery-readiness owns authorization and execution; selection alone grants nothing.

risk_models.name: Dependency and software supply chain
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Trusted source/build/dependency assumptions are wrong, mutable, compromised, incompatible, or unverifiable.
evidence_obligations: Exact versions, sources, generated artifacts, provenance, compatibility, and rollback are bound.
Missing attestations remain gaps.
risk_models.escalation: Dependency decisions require named approval; the method layer cannot authorize manifest/lock/generated changes.

risk_models.name: Unknown causal failure
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Speculative fixes mask the first failure or alter symptoms without identifying the causal path.
evidence_obligations: The first failure and causal signature are preserved.
Experiments distinguish competing hypotheses before repair.
risk_models.escalation: After three failed attempts reopen the upstream model instead of adding a fourth patch.

risk_models.name: AI-agent execution and evaluation assurance
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Agent output appears plausible while context, authority, tool identity, continuity, stochastic variance, or grader health is wrong.
evidence_obligations: Repository truth, model/tool identity, authority, deterministic invariants, and case health are explicit.
Live model evidence is separated from repository-native verification.
risk_models.escalation: Use independent repeated attempts only for decision-useful uncertainty; never optimize a single score as quality.

risk_models.name: High-consequence independent assurance
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Common-mode requirement, design, implementation, or oracle faults survive ordinary review and tests.
evidence_obligations: Independence, assumptions, common-mode risk, and claim-evidence-defeater links are explicit.
Formal or diverse evidence is justified by consequence, not prestige.
risk_models.escalation: Specialist/formal selection requires explicit high-consequence signals, prerequisites, and qualified human/domain ownership.

risk_models.name: AI autonomy exceeds task need or control capacity
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: A model-directed loop or multi-agent system is introduced where a simpler workflow would be safer, cheaper, more observable, and easier to accept.
evidence_obligations: The least-autonomous viable alternative is explicitly compared.
Human and deterministic control functions, escalation, and stop rights are observable.
risk_models.escalation: Remove effect authority or add an independently enforced shield when consequence exceeds demonstrated control capacity.

risk_models.name: Agent partial observability and stale belief
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: The agent commits to a plan from incomplete, conflicting, or stale state while a cheap discriminating observation was available.
evidence_obligations: Facts, inferences, unknowns, freshness, and confidence are separated.
Decision-changing observations invalidate dependent plans rather than being narrated away.
risk_models.escalation: Restrict to reversible action or request authoritative observation when material uncertainty remains.

risk_models.name: Long-horizon open-loop drift
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: A valid initial plan becomes unsafe or irrelevant as repository, tool, environment, or external state changes between steps.
evidence_obligations: Each execution horizon revalidates actual postconditions and outstanding effects.
Replanning preserves the stable end-state contract, explicit stop conditions, and current authority.
risk_models.escalation: Stop at the last verified checkpoint when drift cannot be reconciled without new authority or semantics.

risk_models.name: AI repair overfits visible tests or local context
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: A plausible patch satisfies visible examples while preserving the causal defect, breaking hidden behavior, or exploiting an incomplete oracle.
evidence_obligations: Rejected candidates leave replayable counterexamples.
The accepted repair passes independently derived black-box, white-box, and impact-based obligations without weakening tests.
risk_models.escalation: Reopen the requirement, causal model, or oracle after repeated non-progress rather than stacking another patch.

risk_models.name: Untrusted context controls privileged agent behavior
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Retrieved data, tool output, memory, or embedded instructions silently override trusted intent, disclose data, or trigger privileged effects.
evidence_obligations: Instruction/data origin, precedence, declassification, and privileged sinks are explicit.
Adversarial indirect-injection and confused-deputy cases fail safely under least privilege.
risk_models.escalation: Disable consequential tools and require trusted human confirmation when provenance cannot be enforced.

risk_models.name: Irreversible or partially committed agent side effects
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: A multi-step agent action fails after partial external commitment, leaving duplicates, inconsistent state, lost authority context, or no safe recovery path.
evidence_obligations: Every consequential action is checked before effect and recorded with idempotency and recovery state.
Partial failure, duplicate delivery, compensation failure, and unrecoverable effects have owned dispositions.
risk_models.escalation: Keep actions advisory or human-confirmed until shield, compensation, and reconciliation obligations are met.

risk_models.name: Stochastic agent evaluation lacks causal or statistical validity
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: A score or final-state pass hides unsafe trajectories, infrastructure confounding, repeated-measure dependence, or unjustified certainty.
evidence_obligations: Outcome, trajectory, side effect, recovery, identity, case health, infrastructure failures, and sampling design are reported separately.
Any uncertainty claim states its population, assumptions, sample size, intervals, stopping rule, and drift boundary.
risk_models.escalation: Treat results as descriptive and rely on deterministic contracts when experimental assumptions are unmet.

risk_models.name: Persistent agent memory drifts, leaks, or is poisoned
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Memory crosses user/repository scope, preserves stale conclusions, loses provenance, resists correction/deletion, or is poisoned by untrusted content.
evidence_obligations: Each persisted item has identity, owner, provenance, scope, retention, validation, correction, and deletion behavior.
Cross-scope leakage, poisoning, replay, staleness, and derived-store deletion are challenged.
risk_models.escalation: Disable persistent memory and reconstruct context from authoritative sources when lifecycle controls are incomplete.

risk_models.name: Multi-agent topology and ownership failure
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Parallel agents duplicate work, conflict on mutable state, drop dependencies, amplify common-mode error, or spend more on coordination than they gain.
evidence_obligations: Topology follows task dependencies and communication cost rather than agent count.
Exclusive ownership, interfaces, deadlines, resource leases, root adjudication, failure recovery, and integration evidence are explicit.
risk_models.escalation: Collapse to a single agent or root-assigned sequential slices when ownership or integration cannot be proven.

risk_models.name: Reactive Agent execution and fallback loops
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: A fixed workflow cannot react safely to changing conditions, or an ad-hoc reactive loop hides status, cancellation, retry, and fallback cycles.
evidence_obligations: Condition/action status, tick/lifecycle, fallback, cancellation, retry, and loop termination are explicit.
Trace tests cover changing conditions, stuck actions, late completion, and recovery loops.
risk_models.escalation: Use an explicit state/temporal model when global safety, fairness, or concurrency crosses the reactive tree.

risk_models.name: Stable hierarchical domain planning
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Recurring expert workflows are decomposed inconsistently or illegally because reusable domain methods and ordering constraints are implicit.
evidence_obligations: Abstract/primitive tasks, method applicability, state effects, and ordering are governed domain knowledge.
Generated plans validate against invariants and concrete replay.
risk_models.escalation: Use an ordinary dependency graph when the domain is novel, incomplete, or changing too quickly for governed HTN knowledge.

risk_models.name: Dynamic heterogeneous Agent task allocation
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Changing work is assigned using stale or self-reported capabilities, causing duplicate awards, starvation, overload, failed contractors, or integration mismatch.
evidence_obligations: Announcement, evidence-backed capability, bid, award, timeout, cancellation, completion, and reassignment states are explicit.
Simulation preserves single ownership, bounded allocation, and failure recovery.
risk_models.escalation: Use root-assigned exclusive ownership when static scheduling is sufficient or bid/capability validity cannot be enforced.

risk_models.name: Calibrated selective Agent action
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: A stochastic action threshold claims controlled risk or coverage without independent calibration, explicit loss, abstention behavior, or stable distribution assumptions.
evidence_obligations: Loss, tolerated risk, held-out calibration, exchangeability, sample size, coverage/selectivity, and drift behavior are explicit.
Acceptance data is not reused to tune the claimed threshold.
risk_models.escalation: Use conservative abstention and ordinary validation without a formal coverage claim when calibration assumptions fail.

risk_models.name: Agent simulation and reality-gap risk
risk_models.failure_hypothesis: Unsafe or expensive live trials are replaced by a simulation whose missing fidelity is then mistaken for real-world acceptance.
evidence_obligations: The decision-relevant simulated dimensions are validated against known observations and all reality gaps are explicit.
Simulation rejection/acceptance remains separate from authorized live evidence.
risk_models.escalation: Keep live claims NOT RUN and require an authorized bounded real-world gate when the decision exceeds validated simulation fidelity.
